title: Elodie and the Alibi
premise: When the coffin of Harlan Voss, founder of the fog-bound town of Marrow's Bend, is exhumed for a land dispute, insurance investigator Rosalind Blackwood discovers it empty — and realizes the death certificate matches a case they were forced to close twenty years ago: the disappearance of their foster brother, Danny, whose body was never found. Using their photographic memory to reconstruct the original investigation, Rosalind uncovers that Danny faked his death with Voss's help, and that Voss himself staged his own empty grave to finally escape the town that owned him. In the end, Rosalind must choose between exposing the truth and protecting the found family that helped two people vanish — choosing loyalty, but only after extracting one honest confession from each of them.
about_author: Noor Okafor is a former claims adjuster turned novelist who grew up in a coastal town where everyone knew everyone's business and no one told the truth. Their fiction explores the quiet violence of small-town secrets and the families we build when our own fail us.

chapters.title: The Weight of Empty Earth
chapters.summary: Rosalind Blackwood is called to Marrow's Bend to assess an exhumation tied to a land claim, and watches workers lift a coffin that should hold town founder Harlan Voss — and holds nothing but river stones. POV Rosalind. Emotional beat: professional detachment cracking into unease as the crowd of townsfolk reacts not with shock, but with fear.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Dust
chapters.summary: Digging into records at the county archive, Rosalind's photographic memory snags on the coroner's signature from Voss's death certificate — the same name that signed off on the closed case of their foster brother Danny's drowning in 2004. POV Rosalind, with flashback fragments. Emotional beat: old grief resurfacing, the case everyone swore was closed.

chapters.title: What the Town Remembers
chapters.summary: Rosalind interviews townsfolk who each give contradictory accounts of Voss's final days; the funeral director, Mabel Okonkwo, lies fluently until Rosalind quotes her own testimony back word-for-word. POV alternating between Rosalind and Mabel. Emotional beat: the reader sees Mabel is protecting someone, and Rosalind begins to suspect the whole town conspired.

chapters.title: Danny
chapters.summary: A full flashback chapter: teenage Rosalind and Danny in their last foster home, Danny's plan to run away to the coast, and the morning the river gave up a body wearing Danny's jacket. POV young Rosalind. Emotional beat: devastating tenderness, establishing why this case was never just a case.

chapters.title: The Statute
chapters.summary: Rosalind learns the statute of limitations on the falsified death certificate expires in eleven days, forcing a deadline onto what should be a cold trail. The town council moves to have the empty coffin quietly reburied. POV Rosalind. Emotional beat: mounting pressure and isolation as allies turn bureaucratic and the town closes ranks.

chapters.title: Marrow and Bone
chapters.summary: Following river-stone residue and a boat rental ledger, Rosalind finds a cabin upstream with two sets of dishes, two beds, and a photograph of Voss alive and laughing beside a man whose face is turned away. POV Rosalind. Emotional beat: hope curdling into dread — the turned-away man has Danny's build, Danny's scarred left hand.

chapters.title: Confessions at Low Tide
chapters.summary: Rosalind confronts Mabel, who confesses she helped fake Voss's death because he was dying anyway and wanted to spare the town — and admits Danny didn't drown; the body was a stranger, and Voss sheltered him. POV Mabel, then Rosalind. Emotional beat: relief and fury colliding — Danny is alive, and chose not to come back.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't Buried Twice
chapters.summary: Rosalind tracks Voss to a hospice cottage and finds him dying, lucid, and unrepentant; he reveals Danny stayed nearby for years out of guilt toward Rosalind, too ashamed to return after letting them mourn. POV Rosalind. Emotional beat: the antagonist becomes human, and Rosalind's quest for truth starts to feel like a trap of their own making.

chapters.title: Everything the Water Kept
chapters.summary: Climax: at the riverbank where Danny 'drowned,' Rosalind waits through the night and Danny comes — older, bearded, terrified. He offers the full truth: the stranger's body, Voss's bargain, his cowardice. Rosalind must decide whether to turn him in before the statute expires at dawn. POV alternating Rosalind and Danny. Emotional beat: raw confrontation, love and betrayal in the same breath.

chapters.title: Alibi
chapters.summary: Resolution: Rosalind files a report proving Voss was never murdered and the certificate error died with him, closing the case without naming Danny — then gives Danny one condition: honesty, forever, starting now. The siblings sit together as the sun rises over Marrow's Bend. POV Rosalind. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace; truth served, loyalty kept, family reforged rather than found.
